templates.why_chosen: An explicit boxed legend maps dashed to the management path and solid to the data path, separating the dashed host-side transport region above from the solid NIC hardware (TX Merge, RX Split, Flow Table) below.
templates.what_to_learn: Put a small boxed legend that names dashed as the management path and solid as the data path, then honor it everywhere: dashed for the host-side software containers, solid for the on-chip hardware, and color the two traffic directions (blue send, red receive) only where they physically cross at the net port.

templates.why_chosen: High-confidence nested-stack exemplar where a dashed host-side Application Buffers box nests a GPU HBM box that nests its MR descriptor, mirrored by the NIC's own nested Flow Table to MS List to MR Table chain.
templates.what_to_learn: Carry one indirection chain, table entry to resource, as boxes nested or linked one inside the next rather than a flat row, and put a boxed legend decoding dashed-versus-solid line meaning directly in the frame when both a management path and a data path are drawn.

templates.why_chosen: A NIC floorplan reading: the chip boundary holds TX/RX merge units in the middle with per-flow tables (MS List, Flow Table) at the edge, while host-side GPU HBM sits outside as off-chip memory.
templates.what_to_learn: Draw the NIC's own boundary and put its splitting/merging compute in the middle, per-flow lookup tables at the edge, and the host's off-chip memory (GPU HBM) clearly outside that boundary; keep the boxed dashed-vs-solid legend so a floorplan reader still knows which lines are control.
